title: COMMBAT: a web platform for exploring expression control of biosynthetic gene clusters.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the GitLab repository tree through its API: folders antiSMASH_DB/info (per-genome GCF folders), mibig_gbk_4.0, mibig_json_4.0, matrices (COMMBAT_DB_2023.1, LogoMotif_v_0.1, Prodoric_2021.9, RegPrecise_v_3.2), example_inputs, and seven R/Perl scripts including Calculation_COMMBAT_score.R. Read the README (install and run instructions). No file of experimentally validated TF-BGC (transcription factor to biosynthetic gene cluster) interactions or any labelled table was visible in the tree. Web server responds (HTTP 200). Europe PMC supplementary endpoint timed out.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the COMMBAT score is a hand-designed formula (motif match score times weighted region and gene-function scores); that ~300 experimentally validated TF binding sites from a prior meta-analysis set the weights; 2,278 PWMs (position weight matrices, i.e. binding-motif profiles) in the text vs 'over 4000' in the abstract; 'over 400,000' BGCs from MIBiG and antiSMASH DB; that validated 'reference BGCs' can be highlighted in the web interface.

a1_downloadable.note: Code, motif matrices and public BGC files are openly on GitLab (tree listed via API); no login. Licence file present but not read.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No labelled table exists. The only per-pair output is the COMMBAT score, which you would generate yourself by running the pipeline; true regulatory interactions would have to be assembled from literature (checked repo tree, none found).

a3_inputs_present.note: BGC GenBank/JSON files and PWMs are in the repo, so sequences are present (seen in tree listing, files not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: Scores are unitless normalized ratios per the paper; not an issue for this task (paper text only).

a5_enough_rows.note: Experimentally validated interactions number roughly 300 binding sites per the paper's cited meta-analysis, far under 400; not found as a file, so unverified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; MIBiG subset small, antiSMASH DB scan of 400,000 BGCs large
a6_fits_laptop.note: A MIBiG-only scan would fit; not measured.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Abstract says over 4,000 PWMs, results text says 2,278 PWMs; files not counted, so cannot tell which is right.

a8_label_provenance.note: The scalable 'label' is the COMMBAT score, a deterministic formula computed from the motif and gene-annotation features; learning it is pure distillation and circular.

existing_models.name: COMMBAT score (Ribeiro Monteiro et al., Microbial Genomics 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to outperform sequence-only motif scanning at recovering validated binding sites; exact metric and split not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Binding sites in BGCs diverge from canonical motifs, limiting motif scanning (this paper's abstract).

existing_models.name: iModulon ICA (independent component analysis) of 454 Streptomyces coelicolor transcriptomes (Lee et al., Advanced Science 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Unsupervised; 117 gene modules explaining 81.6% of expression variance, putative regulons for 40 regulators. Not a supervised split.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer or DNABERT-2 (DNA language models) on promoter windows, hypothetically
backbone.hardware: CPU for a few thousand windows

integration.partner_dataset: MIBiG 4.0 (curated BGCs with known products), already bundled
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which environmental signals switch on cryptic antibiotic clusters - but without measured regulation labels the join answers nothing new.

controls.positive_control: Validated reference TF-BGC pairs highlighted in the web interface (count unknown).
controls.negative_control: Shuffled-motif PWMs scanned against the same BGCs.
controls.external_validation: None found; iModulon regulons for S. coelicolor could serve as a partial independent check.

honest_claim_h3: At best: ranks candidate regulator-cluster pairs among a few hundred literature-validated binding sites, mostly from Streptomyces, without any measured negatives.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around antibiotic-making gene clusters to predict which regulatory proteins switch those clusters on.
plain_idea.train_on: DNA windows upstream of genes in bacterial biosynthetic gene clusters paired with a regulator's binding-motif profile; number of truly validated pairs unknown (roughly 300 binding sites per the paper).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the regulator really controls the cluster. The only large-scale answer available is the authors' own formula score, not a measurement; real answers come from scattered lab experiments (binding assays, knockouts).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Natural-product chemists could pick growth conditions or genetic tweaks to wake up silent antibiotic clusters, but only if trained on real measured interactions.

ml_idea: Considered: train a DNA-language-model head to predict validated TF-BGC binding versus background, benchmarked against the COMMBAT score. Blocked because no labelled interaction table is released and the scalable label is the formula itself.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; project rejected at Part A before any compute planning.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count experimentally validated TF-BGC pairs available as a file (from the 2025 Microbial Genomics paper supplement or the web server's reference list); under 400 kills it.

verdict_reason: A tool, not a labelled dataset: the only scalable output is the authors' hand-built COMMBAT formula score (A8 circular), no table of measured interactions is released (A2), and validated binding sites number roughly 300 per the paper (A5).
